--- title: "1. Input data and processing" --- ::: {.cell} ::: The start page of QuaNTA where metadata is provided, data is uploaded, read and processed using the settings provided by the user. All settings and metadata can be saved as a parameters file for ease of reprocessing with new settings or same settings for new data.
## File structure QuaNTA reads a `.txt` file formatted according to the [MS-DIAL](https://systemsomicslab.github.io/compms/msdial/main.html) **alignment result** output format. Upload it as it is, or compressed as `.zip` or `.gz`. The file has two parts: four rows of **sample information** at the top, and below them one row of headers above all **feature** (a compound or an unknown peak) rows with its peak area in every sample. This is the top-left corner of the example file: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Class Blk C0 C0-005 C0-01
File type Blank Standard Standard Standard
Injection order 1 2 3 4
Batch ID 1 1 1 1
Alignment ID Average Rt(min) Average Mz Metabolite name Comment MS/MS spectrum PROCBLK3_B1_1 Cal0_E_B1_2 Cal0-005_E_B1_3 Cal0-01_E_B1_4
16572 13.016 219.17401 (+)-Nootkatone Quant 2698760 0 419457 749115
5569 9.437 136.02139 1,3-benzothiazole Quant 2713850 131522 0 0
19717 8.393 240.14929 1,3-Di-o-tolylguanidine Quant 1685925 0 0 384821
15351 7.449 212.11803 1,3-Diphenylguanidine Quant 100897380 1928345 2064414 2317076
````` ::: :::
### The four sample rows The four sample rows (shaded above) describe each sample column: | Row | Content | In QuaNTA | |---|---|---| | `Class` | the group of the sample, e.g. `Healthy`, `QC1`, `C0-5` | the groups in figures and statistics | | `File type` | `Sample`, `QC`, `Standard` or `Blank` | study sample, QC, calibration sample or method blank | | `Injection order` | a number | the order along the sequence (drift, figures over the sequence) | | `Batch ID` | a number | blank subtraction and calibration per batch | ### The feature columns QuaNTA needs these feature columns (exact names): `Alignment ID`, `Average Rt(min)`, `Average Mz`, `Metabolite name` and `Comment`. Other columns are ignored. ### Naming conventions The **`Comment`** column tells QuaNTA what each feature is: | Comment | Meaning | |---|---| | `Quant` | a targeted compound, quantified with a calibration curve | | `Quant\` | a targeted compound with a compound class after the backslash, e.g. `Quant\ATZ` | | `IS` | an isotope-labelled internal standard | | `IS\` | an internal standard with a compound class, e.g. `IS\ATZ` | | `vIS` | the volumetric internal standard (added to check and correct the volume) | | `R` | removed from the data when it is read | | empty or anything else | a non-targeted feature | The **calibration samples** (`File type` = `Standard`) carry their concentration in the sample name, after `Cal`, with a dash for the decimal point: `Cal0` (the zero calibrant), `Cal0-005` (0.005), `Cal0-5` (0.5), `Cal10` (10). **QC samples** with the same `Class` are replicates of one QC material; several QC materials (e.g. `QC-low`, `QC-high`) are possible. ### Example dataset The example dataset provided with the QuaNTA app is completely synthetic and has 196 targeted compounds, 22 internal standards, 1 volumetric internal standard and 1000 non-targeted features, measured in 299 samples in 3 batches. ::: {.callout-warning} ## Check before uploading When you click **Process data**, QuaNTA lists `Comment` values that do not follow the conventions (e.g. `quant`, `IS-ATZ`) and column names that look like the required ones but are not exact (e.g. `Comment2`). Values that look like `Quant` or `IS` are shown in red: they would be treated as non-targeted. Fix them in MS-DIAL or in the file and upload again. ::: ## Uploading and reading The initial page has 3 sections: Input and metadata, reading and processing data and logs ![Starting page of app when opened.](images/page1-start.png){.screenshot} ### Upload file, read and process 1. If the user has previously saved a parameters file it contains metadata, processing settings and which dataset was uploaded at the time of saving it. 2. Otherwise, fill in metadata (optional), choose a `.txt`, `.zip` or `.gz` (containing a `.txt` file) by clicking "Browse" in lower left corner 3. Choose whether to process batch-wise or globally and read file by clicking "Read data file".
Section 2 is now viewable. ![Example parameters file and data loaded and read.](images/page1-read.png){.screenshot} ## Processing settings The settings are grouped as in the app. Hover the ⓘ next to each in the app for the full explanation; options that the data cannot support (e.g. a volumetric IS option without a vIS) are greyed out. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: :::
### Processing data 4. Having chosen your processing settings click **Process data**. A popup will warn you of any problems detected in the raw data. ![The popup before processing, with a note on the columns of the example file.](images/page1-process-popup.png){.screenshot width="75%"} 5. Click **Proceed** to start. The *Processing log* on the right shows the progress; when it ends with "Finished.", pages 3 and 4 show the results. ![Processing finished: the processing log on the right.](images/page1-processed.png){.screenshot} ::: {.callout-tip} ## Save your settings **Download settings (.yml)** saves metadata, processing settings and the name of the dataset. :::
